_schema.purpose: Single canonical register of everything this project has measured, refuted, or left untried. Machine-readable source of truth; FINDINGS.md is GENERATED from it by findings.py and must never be hand-edited.

fields.kind: law | lever | dead_end | contradiction | untried | external
fields.claim: one sentence, falsifiable, stated as what is true
fields.magnitude: the number that matters, with units
fields.evidence: prereg number, file:line, or external source
fields.scope: the hardware and model class the claim was measured on - a claim outside its scope is a guess
fields.status: established | shipped | refuted | open | staked | untested
fields.wired_into: where it reaches shipped code, or null

untried_extra_fields.predicted_effect: staked magnitude - written BEFORE the test, so a miss is visible
untried_extra_fields.why_it_is_promising: which established finding implies this lever should work

_schema.reference_box: i5-7600K, GTX 1060 6GB, 16GB DDR4-3000, SATA MX500, PCIe 3.0 x16 @ 12.2 GB/s

laws.claim: Decode speed is bandwidth-bound: tok/s = eta(tier) x BW / active-bytes-per-token.
laws.scope: VRAM/RAM/disk tiers, dense and MoE, one GPU

laws.claim: KV cache is a first-class bandwidth consumer priced at its own efficiency, ETA_KV = 0.70.
laws.magnitude: tg32 20.35 -> 6.30 tok/s from d0 to d16384

laws.claim: Quantization fragility is measurable but NOT predictable from architecture; attention and SSM tensors are fragile, embeddings and FFN are not.
laws.magnitude: depth-aware recipe protects attn_.*/ssm_.* (+shexp/nextn on MoE)

laws.claim: Effective rank, not bit-count, is the state variable of quantization; incoherence is rank-conditional.
laws.magnitude: gauge hypothesis refuted; cache phase-transition observed

laws.claim: Prefill is compute-bound, so the bit ladder runs BACKWARDS there - fewer bits is SLOWER.
laws.wired_into: documented; planner does not yet model prefill bits

laws.claim: The VRAM claimants - weights, KV cache, compute buffer - are FUNGIBLE, and fungibility is placement-specific: only a configuration that is actually starved can spend the refund.
laws.magnitude: evicting KV recovers 2.42x prefill on the split, and nothing (-3%) on all-experts-to-CPU

laws.claim: There is no single best placement - there is a Pareto frontier selected by the prompt:generation ratio.
laws.magnitude: 1.33x between best and worst choice across chat/coding/RAG/document-QA

laws.claim: llama.cpp's CUDA compute buffer is exactly linear in the ubatch, so demand grows smoothly while VRAM supply ends abruptly - producing a cliff, not a taper.
laws.magnitude: 0.5874 MiB per ubatch token, to four figures; -45% prefill in one -ub step

laws.claim: ggml offers host-resident weights to CUDA once the ubatch clears 32 tokens, so host weights cross PCIe once per UBATCH rather than once per token.
laws.magnitude: +73% prefill at ub 512 -> 2048 with experts on CPU

laws.claim: The Gemma MLP weight element stream is white - there is no intra-tensor redundancy for VQ to exploit.

levers.claim: Partial MoE expert offload (-ot blk.(K..N).ffn_.*_exps.=CPU --no-mmap) beats both all-VRAM and all-CPU.
Sizing -ub from measured VRAM headroom (never pinning it) is worth up to 73% of prefill and avoids a 45% cliff.
levers.magnitude: 199.90 -> 345.89 where it applies; -45% where it does not

levers.claim: Evicting KV to host RAM (-nkvo 1) buys prefill on a VRAM-starved placement and costs decode.
levers.magnitude: 3.84x prefill on the split; -47% decode at 16k depth

levers.claim: N-gram speculation (--spec-type ngram-simple) more than doubles code decode at zero download and identical output.
Depth-aware protection of fragile tensors buys quality at near-zero size.
The probe's band search beats APEX's symmetric prior: real fragility is strictly monotonic and LATE-weighted, not symmetric across depth.
levers.magnitude: S-1 HIT sharper than staked (reference PPL 5.4298, WikiText, 40-layer source); out-of-domain rematch confirms calibration generalises - 25.6% on KL against the Q8_0 parent, on a corpus the imatrix never saw

levers.claim: Dense models have a measurable PROTECTED share of activated bytes - the attention tensors that stay high-precision - so dense speed responds to bit-width instead of being flat in it.
levers.magnitude: DENSE_PROTECTED_SHARE = 0.214, the mean attention share read from GGUF tensor shapes: 10.8% Qwen2.5-7B, 20.2% gemma4-12B, 25.1% Qwen3.5-4B, 29.6% Qwen3-0.6B
levers.evidence: prereg #17 (dense-activation-model) - P-1 HIT, P-2 HIT decisively, P-3 MISS

dead_ends.claim: Reducing expert count (top-k 8->4) for DECODE is strictly dominated by simply quantizing further.
dead_ends.magnitude: k=4: 1.335x speed for 1.206x perplexity. Bit ladder: 1.424x for 1.048x - faster AND 4x cheaper.

dead_ends.claim: Intra-tensor VQ on Gemma MLP weights cannot pay - the stream is white.
k-means matched-rate VQ is a runtime trap - decode cost swamps the compression win.
Two frontier cells are dominated on BOTH axes and must never be recommended.
dead_ends.magnitude: all-experts-CPU + KV evicted 336.31/15.82; split + KV VRAM + ub2048 163.39/20.13

dead_ends.claim: Forking or patching llama.cpp is not worth it in the VRAM/host-resident regimes - a PERFECT custom runtime buys single-digit percent.
dead_ends.scope: EXPLICITLY NOT the disk-streaming tier - ds4 shows ~7x there

dead_ends.claim: The sub-4-bit decode collapse is a FORMAT property, not a bit-width property - gating on bits was wrong.

contradictions.claim: MODELS['glm-744b']['kvp'] = 188416 is 30-60x too large, making GLM-family predictions wrong.
contradictions.next_action: read GLM-5.2's actual attention architecture; do NOT back-solve from a datapoint

contradictions.claim: The law under-predicts the MOST COMMON configuration - a model that simply fits in VRAM - by up to +81%, because eta is a property of the QUANTIZATION FORMAT CLASS and the law treats it as one constant across all formats.
contradictions.magnitude: 13 all-in-VRAM points across three sessions. By format class: sub-4-bit (Q2_K, IQ3_XS, IQ3_M) eta = 0.425 / 0.436 / 0.443 - FLAT within 4% while bytes per token move 13%. 4-bit (Q4_K_M) eta = 0.510 (4B) and 0.631 (7B), with prereg #15 independently measuring 0.461 and 0.560 for the same two. The law assumes 0.35 for all of them.
contradictions.evidence: prereg #24 (eta-vram-bytes-per-token) + prereg #15 (law4-v3-overhead-term) + weights/data/prereg24_eta_bytes_per_token.log; verify.py layer 3 FAILS on this
contradictions.wired_into: disclosed in CLI output as 'a floor, not a ceiling' - but the disclosed band (2%-67%) is itself now too narrow
contradictions.why_it_is_the_top_item: It is the placement most users land on, it is the one we undersell, and underselling -ngl 99 pushes people toward complicated offload placements that are actually SLOWER for them. Every other finding in this register is about configurations that are harder than the default.
contradictions.what_the_data_rules_out: (a) FIXED OVERHEAD - refuted decisively by prereg #15. (b) GPU CLOCK STATE - cold 144.21 vs warm 143.37, a hypothesis stated before the test and refuted by it. (c) GATE MODEL-SELECTION - the 7B misses by MORE than the 0.5B. (d) BYTES PER TOKEN AS THE PRIMARY AXIS - refuted by prereg #24's control point, which has FEWER bytes per token than every sub-4-bit 7B point (3.25 vs 3.76-4.26) and a HIGHER eta (0.510 vs 0.425-0.443). That ordering is impossible if bytes drive eta. Note this also overturns my own reading earlier the same day, when arm A's monotonicity looked like support for the bytes axis - it is confounded, because within one architecture bytes and bit-width rise together.
contradictions.leading_hypothesis: TWO factors, neither sufficient alone. (1) FORMAT CLASS sets the level: at matched bytes, 4-bit kernels run far closer to peak bandwidth than sub-4-bit ones, plausibly because sub-4-bit dequantisation costs more compute per byte delivered. (2) WITHIN a format, eta still rises with size - Q4_K_M 0.510 -> 0.631 here, 0.461 -> 0.560 in #15, same direction both sessions.
contradictions.next_action: BLOCKED on the layer-4 anchor audit, which must run first: if any anchor is all-in-VRAM and currently retrodicted correctly, it is in direct conflict with a +81% miss on the same tier and THAT conflict is the result. After that, a per-format eta needs a SECOND GPU before any published number moves - every point here is one memory system, and '4-bit kernels use it better' is a hypothesis about a GTX 1060. Between-session drift of 10-13% with sub-1% within-session error bars (prereg #24 P-3) means no fit may cross a session boundary.
contradictions.also_establishes: Between-session drift is 10-13% on decode against sub-1% within-session error bars, now measured three times on the same 4B model: 27.30 (07-26), 30.89 (07-27 early), 30.03 (07-27 late). C-04 recorded this for prefill; it holds for decode too, and it bounds what any single session can conclude.

contradictions.claim: verify.py layer 3 is sensitive to GPU clock state - the same 0.5B model measures across the +/-25% band depending on whether the card is warm.
contradictions.scope: verify layer 3 on the smallest model
contradictions.next_action: either fix the clock state before measuring, or stop selecting the smallest model - a 0.5B decode is overhead-dominated and is the worst possible test of a bandwidth law

contradictions.claim: Absolute prefill figures are not stable across invocation shapes, only ratios are.
contradictions.magnitude: split/nkvo0/ub2048 measured 85.47 swept alone vs 161.59 in the full matrix
contradictions.next_action: any future use of an absolute figure needs its own controlled run

contradictions.claim: A recurring failure mode has now bitten this project twice: a quantity assumed CONSTANT across quantization formats turns out to be a property OF the format.
contradictions.magnitude: D-06 (the sub-4-bit decode collapse was format-dependent, not bit-width-dependent) and C-02 (eta is format-class-dependent, not constant)
contradictions.wired_into: nothing yet - this is a lint waiting to be written
contradictions.next_action: Audit EVERY remaining constant in plan.py for the same assumption, before a user finds the third instance. ETA_KV = 0.70 is the obvious next candidate: it was fitted without varying the KV cache TYPE, and register entry U-01 is about to vary exactly that. If the pattern holds a third time it stops being a coincidence and becomes something the five-layer gate should test for directly.

untried.claim: KV cache quantization (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0) is the cheapest way to free the fungible claimant.
untried.hypothesis: Halving KV bytes frees VRAM that L-06 proves converts directly into compute-buffer headroom, so it should buy BOTH decode (fewer KV bytes to re-read, L-02) and prefill (bigger safe ubatch, L-08) at once - the only lever we know of that pays on both axes.
untried.predicted_effect: at 16k depth: decode +20% to +40%; safe ubatch one step larger; may make -nkvo 1 unnecessary entirely
untried.why_it_is_promising: L-02 + L-06 + L-08 jointly imply it, and we have never tested it
untried.protocol: llama-bench -ctk/-ctv {f16,q8_0,q4_0} x -d {0,16384} x {split, all-CPU}; measure perplexity cost separately before shipping

untried.claim: MoE expert routing is skewed, so frequency-ranked expert residency beats the contiguous blk-range split we currently ship.
untried.hypothesis: Our split assigns experts to VRAM by LAYER INDEX, which is arbitrary with respect to how often each expert is actually selected. Ranking experts by measured activation frequency and pinning the hot ones should dominate a contiguous range at identical VRAM cost.
untried.predicted_effect: +15% to +40% decode at the same VRAM budget, IF routing entropy is well below uniform
untried.why_it_is_promising: PowerInfer's hot/cold neuron result is the dense analogue and it is large; our split is currently index-based purely because that is what -ot regexes address
untried.protocol: instrument expert selection counts over a representative corpus; build an -ot regex from the top-N experts; compare against the contiguous split at matched VRAM

untried.claim: Page-locked (pinned) host memory raises the effective PCIe rate for host-resident expert tensors.
untried.hypothesis: Pageable host memory forces the driver through a staging buffer. Our whole host-resident regime is priced at 12.2 GB/s; if that figure is a pageable-memory artifact, the ceiling on every -ot placement moves.
untried.predicted_effect: up to +30% on host-resident prefill if currently pageable; 0% if llama.cpp already pins
untried.why_it_is_promising: it would move a constant that every host-resident prediction depends on
untried.protocol: first READ llama.cpp's host buffer allocation path to see whether it already uses cudaHostAlloc; only measure if it does not

untried.claim: Prompt/prefix cache reuse dwarfs every placement lever on RAG and document-QA workloads.
untried.hypothesis: L-07 says document-QA (200:1) is the workload where placement matters most. But a reused prefix skips prefill ENTIRELY, which is not a percentage improvement - it is a different asymptote.
untried.predicted_effect: 10x+ on repeated-prefix workloads; 0x on fresh prompts
untried.why_it_is_promising: our frontier optimises the cost of doing prefill; this avoids it
untried.protocol: llama-server with --prompt-cache / slot restore; measure time-to-first-token on repeated vs fresh prefixes

untried.claim: Batch>1 (parallel slots) changes which placement wins, because it amortises host-weight transfer across concurrent requests.
untried.hypothesis: L-09 says host weights cross PCIe once per ubatch. Concurrent slots fill ubatches that a single stream cannot, so the all-experts-to-CPU placement should improve superlinearly with slot count while all-in-VRAM stays flat.
untried.predicted_effect: the frontier reorders at -np 4; aggregate throughput +2x to +4x on the offloaded placements
untried.why_it_is_promising: every measurement in this project is -np 1, so an entire dimension is unexplored
untried.protocol: llama-bench/llama-server at -np {1,2,4,8} across the three frontier rows; report aggregate AND per-request rates

untried.claim: The disk-streaming tier has ~7x available that our fork verdict (D-05) explicitly does not cover.
untried.hypothesis: D-05 concluded a custom runtime buys 1-6%, but scoped that to the VRAM/host-resident regimes. antirez/ds4 reports order-of-magnitude gains on streaming, where the bottleneck is I/O scheduling rather than bandwidth accounting.
untried.predicted_effect: unknown; the point is that our own verdict has a hole in it
untried.why_it_is_promising: it is the one regime where we have already said our no-fork conclusion does not apply
untried.protocol: reproduce ds4's approach on the reference box's SATA MX500; compare against our stream-from-disk tier

untried.claim: Asymmetric top-k (k=4 to ingest, k=8 to generate) survives Stage 1 and needs Stage 2.
untried.hypothesis: D-01 killed top-k for decode. Prereg #22 showed the PREFILL prize reaches every shipped placement at +21% to +63%. The open question is whether the +20.6% perplexity cost attaches to ingestion or only to generation.
untried.predicted_effect: if the cost is generation-only, asymmetric top-k is real and ships as an upstream PR, never a fork
untried.why_it_is_promising: prereg #22 Stage 1 passed its own kill rule
untried.protocol: slot save/restore between a k=4 and a k=8 server; measure perplexity attributable to each phase

untried.claim: A draft MODEL (not n-gram) extends V-04's 2.10x from code to prose.
untried.hypothesis: ngram-simple gains nothing on prose (1.01x) because it drafts by copying spans from context. A small draft model generalises where copying cannot.
untried.predicted_effect: 1.5x to 2x on prose decode, at the cost of VRAM for the draft model - which L-06 says competes with everything else
untried.why_it_is_promising: V-04 is our largest single measured decode win and it currently only fires on one content type
untried.protocol: Qwen2.5-0.5B as draft for a 7B target; sweep draft length; the VRAM cost must be charged against the frontier, not ignored

external.why: The closest prior art to our entire MoE offload thesis - heterogeneous CPU/GPU MoE inference with explicit expert placement. If they have solved expert residency we should adopt rather than rediscover.
external.question_to_answer: How do they choose WHICH experts stay resident? Index-based like ours, or frequency-based like U-02?

external.why: Hot/cold neuron residency driven by measured activation frequency - the dense analogue of U-02, and the strongest published evidence that frequency-ranked placement beats index-ranked.
external.question_to_answer: What is the measured routing/activation skew, and does it hold for MoE experts as well as dense neurons?

external.why: Reported ~7x on the disk-streaming tier - the one regime our no-fork verdict (D-05) does not cover.
external.question_to_answer: Is the gain I/O scheduling, or a different quantization? See U-06.

external.why: A GLM-5.2 deployment at known hardware - the datapoint that could close C-01 without back-solving.
external.question_to_answer: What attention architecture does the config declare? That is the input C-01 needs.

external.why: Paged attention and automatic prefix caching are the production form of U-04.
external.question_to_answer: What hit rate does prefix caching achieve on RAG-shaped workloads, and what is the memory overhead of paging?
